A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Prompt-CAM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G support comparison, including matching content across the changed title and numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and faithfulness experiments, qualitative analyses, and a 35-participant human study, including additional results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised numerical results, an additional evaluated comparator, and revised qualitative examples.

M1.justification: v2 removes the optional focused pairwise variant from v1 Section 3.4, which restricted inference to the ground-truth and reference-class prompts. The core Shallow/Deep architectures, shared classifier, cross-entropy objective, and greedy attention-head ranking remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The same 13 datasets and classification, trait-localization, trait-manipulation, and taxonomic applications remain. Removing Bird and Insects examples from Figure 4 does not remove those datasets from evaluation. The focused variant's removal concerns an inference configuration within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds attention roll-out as an evaluated faithfulness comparator alongside Grad-CAM, Layer-CAM, and Eigen-CAM. The linear-probing comparison and qualitative comparisons with INTR, ProtoPFormer, TesNet, and ProtoConcepts remain.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation drops the two-prompt pairwise testing configuration used in v1 Figure 9. Retained experiments preserve the stated splits, sample counts, backbones, training settings, metrics, and human-study design. The expanded faithfulness description documents additional details without establishing a changed calculation.

E4.justification: v2 removes the focused comparison investigating how required traits change with reference-species similarity. It replaces the Figure 8 counterfactual example and adds a Scott Oriole masking illustration in Figure 1. Appendix analyses of prompt placement, head masking, errors, and backbone variants remain.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged: the numerical tables provide point estimates, and the human study reports the same averaged recognition percentages. No repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 5 revise several scores: Eigen-CAM insertion/deletion changes from 0.42/0.33 to 0.56/0.22, and DINO Prompt-CAM CUB accuracy from 71.9% to 73.2%. Attention roll-out results are added. Figure 8 replaces the input example and its post-manipulation prediction, from Bronzed Cowbird to Boat-tailed Grackle; this is not a changed prediction on an identical image. Human-study percentages remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and the simplified argument contrasting shared and class-specific classification weights remain mathematically unchanged. Rewording and changing a greedy-search head index from r to r′ do not introduce new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: a simple interpretable adaptation of pretrained ViTs, class-specific trait localization, broad empirical applicability, and taxonomic extensions. The changed title and revised wording do not materially alter these claims.

C2.justification: v2 removes the qualification that predicting against all classes may overlook subtle differences between the closest categories, together with the prompt-subsampling explanation offered to address it. The interpretability–accuracy tradeoff and limitations caused by invisible or unclear traits remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds code/demo access information, explicitly identifies DINO as the default backbone, and explains that faithfulness evaluation ranks pixels using attention maps aggregated over top heads. These are documentation additions; appendix training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to TransCAM, Visual Query Tuning, and Learning to Prompt for Vision-Language Models. This modestly expands attribution and prompting context while retaining the substantive positioning relative to VPT, INTR, and prototype-based interpretability methods.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, edits the abstract and portions of the introduction and results, and removes the brief standalone main-text Related Work section while retaining Appendix A. Most method exposition and appendix prose remain unchanged apart from references and numbering.

P2.justification: The main-paper visual organization is substantially revised: Figure 1 becomes a full-width, multi-panel overview; Figure 4 shrinks from eight dataset examples to six; Figure 5 shrinks from four error cases to two; the focused-comparison figure disappears; and the taxonomy figure moves onto the final main-text page. Table 1 also gains a comparator row and explicit method labeling.

improvement.justification: The added attention-roll-out comparison and clearer faithfulness procedure modestly strengthen assessment of the central interpretability claim; the overview and code/demo access information also help. These gains are tempered by newly inconsistent classification reporting: v2 gives DINO Bird accuracy as 98.8% in Table 2 versus 98.2% in Table 5, while appendix prose retains 71.9% CUB accuracy despite the tables reporting 73.2%.
